model.name: Risk / Control
model.purpose: Provide an embeddable field group that binds one risk assessment context to a referenced risk, links it to referenced controls and their cited effectiveness determinations, and explains the residual position against referenced appetite or tolerance, without owning the risk entity, the control register or any treatment workflow.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-027 is a mixin: a reusable set of fields attached to a host record so that record can carry a defensible, revision-pinned risk assessment context. It owns the reference and binding fields (risk reference and exact revision, objective/asset/process/context anchors, source-event-consequence anchors), the pinned assessment frame (category and taxonomy pins, scope, exclusions, time horizon, criteria set, method and technique with versions, expression mode), the estimate slots (likelihood and consequence dimension declarations, inherent estimate with its exclusion statement, residual estimate with change explanation), the evidential basis (assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind, uncertainty and confidence qualification), the control-linkage references (relied-on control references and the effectiveness determinations cited for them), the governance stamps at assessment-context level (assessor, context owner, reviewer and acceptance-decision references, review-due timing), and the comparability surface (comparability verdicts, aggregation caveats, scenario dependence). It does not evaluate controls, does not run assessments, does not set or enforce appetite, does not grant acceptance or authorization, and does not define the internals of any pinned technique. Storage and interface are projections: the same field semantics must survive JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB representations.
in_scope: Reference to one risk or opportunity entity together with an exact revision or version pin of the assessed statement.
Anchor references the assessment is scoped against: objectives, assets, processes, organizational units, contextual conditions and applicable jurisdiction or site.
Causal-chain references: risk source or threat source, the event or event class quantified, and the consequences included or explicitly excluded.
Category values with an explicit taxonomy scheme identifier and version pin.
Assessment scope statement, exclusions, likelihood time horizon, as-of time of the assessed state, recording time and validity or review-due time.
Criteria set, assessment method and technique pins with their versions, plus the expression mode (qualitative, ordinal, semi-quantitative, quantitative, probabilistic, scenario-based).
Likelihood and consequence dimension declarations with units, scale references, distribution parameters and support for multi-dimensional impact.
Inherent (pre-control) estimate together with an explicit statement of what 'inherent' excluded in this context, or a documented ground for omitting it.
Assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind, analysis constraints and identification of critical assumptions.
Uncertainty representation, confidence or data-quality grading, unmeasurable aspects and precision caveats.
Control linkage: references to the controls relied on and to the effectiveness determinations cited for them, produced by the owning control assessment model.
Residual (post-control) estimate, the characterization state marking it as adjusted rather than initial, the changed-dimension set and the explanation of change.
References to the appetite or tolerance statement in force and the recorded outcome of comparing the residual estimate against it.
Assessment-context governance stamps: assessor, context owner, reviewer and acceptance-decision references, and review-due timing.
Comparability verdicts, mismatched-pin reporting, aggregation caveats, scenario identifiers and reference-case designation.
out_of_scope: The risk or opportunity entity itself: its identity, statement, status, register membership and lifecycle transitions.
The control register: control identity, design, implementation records, control ownership and control lifecycle.
Evaluation or testing of control design or operating effectiveness and the production of effectiveness determinations.
Risk treatment options, treatment plans, milestones, remediation tracking, plan-of-action records and closure.
Incidents, realized loss events, issues, near misses and post-event investigation.
Objective, asset, process and organizational-unit master data.
Setting, approving, publishing or enforcing risk appetite and tolerance thresholds.
Granting acceptance, authorization or exception decisions on a residual position.
Assessment execution, observation capture and evidence collection procedures.
Audit-trail storage, log integrity and retention execution.
Technique internals and algorithm semantics of any pinned method, including simulation, fault-tree, event-tree and Bayesian computation.
Any fixed numeric risk matrix, default likelihood band, default impact scale or universal scoring rule.
Runtime evaluation or enforcement of thresholds by a policy engine.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-KNW-015 risk / opportunity entity and lifecycle
boundary_notes.distinction: The parent model owns risk identity, statement, register status and lifecycle. This mixin attaches one assessment context to a pinned revision of that entity, carries no risk status transitions, and marks its own binding as stale when the pinned revision is superseded upstream.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Control implementation records and control assessment determinations
boundary_notes.distinction: This mixin stores control references and cites effectiveness determinations by reference; determining, testing or re-opening effectiveness belongs to the control assessment model, where assessment objectives, methods and satisfied / other-than-satisfied determinations are produced.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Risk treatment, remediation and plan-of-action records
boundary_notes.distinction: A residual estimate is an input to treatment planning. Treatment option selection, milestones, scheduling, cost tracking and closure are owned by the treatment model and are not represented here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Assessment execution, observation and evidence records
boundary_notes.distinction: Observations and evidence are cited as the basis of an estimate. Collecting evidence, executing assessment procedures and logging assessment results are owned by the assessment-results model; this mixin holds references and a basis statement only.

The mixin references a versioned tolerance statement and records the comparison outcome. Determining appetite, approving tolerance lines and enforcing them are enterprise governance acts held elsewhere.

Accepting a residual position is an authorization act performed by a designated official and recorded in an authorization or decision model. This mixin carries only a reference to that decision and never grants, derives or enforces it.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Incident, loss event and issue records
boundary_notes.distinction: A realized event is not an assessment. Loss data may be cited as an information source for an estimate, but event records, their timelines and their consequences are owned by event models.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Risk assessment technique definitions (IEC 31010 technique catalogue and comparable method registries)
boundary_notes.distinction: The mixin pins which technique and version were applied and stores the technique's declared outputs. It never restates, parameterizes or re-implements the technique's internal semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Alternative subject kind: relationship (a first-class risk-to-control association)
boundary_notes.distinction: Modelling this as a relationship was tested. A relationship entry would give each risk-control link its own identity, which suits relied-on-control attribution. It fails for the rest of the required content: assessment scope, horizon, criteria pin, likelihood and consequence dimensions, uncertainty and appetite comparison are properties of an assessment context attached to a host record, and one context routinely cites many controls and many consequences. The mixin kind is retained; the residual-change attribution is the part a Dimension may legitimately reify as a separate association record without altering this field group.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-30 Revision 1, Guide for Conducting Risk Assessments
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Primary source for the generic risk model components (threat source, threat event, vulnerability, predisposing condition, likelihood of initiation, likelihood of adverse impact, level of impact), the quantitative / qualitative / semi-quantitative assessment approaches, the threat-, asset-impact- and vulnerability-oriented analysis approaches, the requirement to document purpose, scope, assumptions, constraints, information sources, risk model and analytic approach, and the treatment of residual risk and confidence.

sources.title: NIST Interagency Report 8286 Revision 1, Integrating Cybersecurity and Enterprise Risk Management (ERM)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Primary source for risk register field semantics (risk identifier, description, category, likelihood, impact, exposure, response type, response cost, risk owner, status), the risk detail record as supporting documentation, and the published risk register and risk detail record schemas used as an alignment target.

sources.title: NIST Interagency Report 8286A Revision 1, Identifying and Estimating Cybersecurity Risk for Enterprise Risk Management
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Primary source for the distinction and use of risk tolerance and risk appetite, for documenting likelihood and impact of threat scenarios in registers, and for the schema-level definition of risk register and risk detail record elements.

sources.title: NIST Interagency Report 8286C Revision 1, Staging Cybersecurity Risks for Enterprise Risk Management and Governance Oversight
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Primary source for integrating multiple risk registers into an enterprise risk register and risk profile, and therefore for the roll-up and normalization surface that the comparability check in this model constrains.

sources.title: OSCAL Assessment Results Model v1.1.2 JSON Format Metaschema Reference
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (OSCAL project)
sources.relevance: Primary machine-readable schema for a risk assembly (uuid, title, description, statement, status, origin, threat-id, characterization, mitigating-factor, deadline, remediation, risk-log, related-observation), for characterization with origin and facets (name, system, value), for mitigating factors linked to implementation statements, and for findings that bind a target objective status to associated risks.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-53A Revision 5, Assessing Security and Privacy Controls in Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Primary evidence that control assessment procedures, objectives and determinations are owned by a distinct assessment model, establishing the boundary that this mixin cites effectiveness determinations rather than producing them.

sources.title: The Orange Book: Management of Risk - Principles and Concepts
sources.relevance: Primary public-authority source for risk as the effect of uncertainty on objectives expressed through causes, events and consequences; for risk appetite; for control defined as processes and conditions that maintain or modify risk; for an example category taxonomy; for likelihood-and-consequence analysis against common risk criteria using qualitative, quantitative or combined approaches; and for assurance and three-lines role separation.

sources.title: IEC 31010:2019 Risk management - Risk assessment techniques
sources.organization: International Electrotechnical Commission (published jointly with ISO)
sources.relevance: Catalogue-level primary confirmation of the standard that governs selection and application of risk assessment techniques under uncertainty, of its joint ISO/IEC status and its relationship to ISO 31000. Used to justify pinning a named technique and version by reference rather than defining technique semantics locally. Full normative text is paywalled and no clause-level claim is made.

sources.title: Risk Taxonomy (O-RT), Version 3.1 (Document C251)
sources.relevance: Publication-level primary confirmation of a standard definition and taxonomy for information security risk, companion to the Risk Analysis (O-RA) Standard Version 2.1, used to justify supporting a loss-frequency-and-magnitude decomposition as one pinnable expression mode rather than the universal one. Taxonomy factor detail was not read from the standard text and no clause-level claim is made.

sources.title: NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Primary source for risk measurement challenges (variable risk tolerance, prioritization difficulty, emergent and hard-to-predict risks, plurality of valid measurement approaches), for documenting risk tolerance explicitly, and for the requirement to document and disclose residual risk to downstream users.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-37 Revision 2, Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
sources.relevance: Primary source establishing that control selection, implementation, assessment and authorization are linked but separately accountable processes, and that senior officials make risk decisions on the basis of assessed results, supporting the boundary that acceptance and authorization are referenced rather than owned here.

sources.title: Article 9: Risk Management System, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
sources.organization: Future of Life Institute (AI Act Explorer republication of the Official Journal text)
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; provisions applicable from 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 for the categories referenced
sources.relevance: Legislative text accessed via republication because the EUR-Lex host was not retrievable. Used only as a scoped jurisdictional projection evidencing a legal requirement that risk management measures ensure the relevant residual risk associated with each hazard is judged acceptable, and that estimation and evaluation cover both intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse.

sources.title: Guidance on Enterprise Risk Management - Enterprise Risk Management: Integrating with Strategy and Performance
sources.organization: Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO)
sources.relevance: First-party identification of the 2017 enterprise risk management framework and its freely available executive summary, used to support that a portfolio or profile view and an appetite construct exist as an independent framework family whose vocabulary must be referenced by version rather than assumed. Framework text was not consulted and no principle-level claim is made.

bundles.name: Risk subject binding and assessment framing
bundles.description: Everything that fixes what was assessed and under which declared frame: the referenced risk and its exact revision, the anchors the assessment is scoped against, the causal chain quantified, the category and taxonomy pins, the scope and horizon, and the criteria, method and expression-mode pins.
bundles.rationale: A recorded level of risk is uninterpretable and non-comparable without the reference it belongs to and the frame it was produced under. NIST SP 800-30 requires the purpose, scope, assumptions, constraints, information sources, risk model and analytic approach to be documented alongside results, and IEC 31010 exists precisely because technique choice changes what a result means. Binding fields therefore precede estimate fields.

layers.name: Referenced risk, anchors and causal chain
layers.description: Reference-carrying fields that attach one assessment context to a pinned risk revision, to the objectives, assets, processes and contextual conditions it is scoped against, and to the risk source, event and consequences it quantifies.

findings.name: Referenced risk identity and exact revision pin
findings.description: Identifies which risk or opportunity entity this assessment context is bound to and which exact revision of its statement was assessed, so an estimate cannot silently drift when the referenced statement is later restated. The referenced entity's own status and lifecycle stay with the owning risk model; only the local binding validity state is held here.

questions.text: Which authoritative identifier designates the risk entity that this assessment context is bound to?
answer_data: assigning authority or system of record

questions.text: Which exact revision or version of the referenced risk statement was assessed?
answer_data: content digest of the assessed statement

questions.text: How is this assessment context marked once the pinned risk revision is superseded upstream?
Does the bound subject represent a threat, an opportunity, or both, and where is that reading declared?
answer_data: reference to the statement establishing polarity

data_elements.name: risk-reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the risk or opportunity entity in its owning model.

data_elements.name: risk-revision-pin
data_elements.description: Exact revision, version token or immutable snapshot identifier of the assessed risk statement.

data_elements.name: risk-statement-digest
data_elements.description: Content digest of the assessed statement, allowing detection of upstream change without re-reading the source.

data_elements.name: binding-validity-state
data_elements.description: Local state of the binding: current, superseded-upstream, dangling or withdrawn. Describes this record only, never the referenced risk's own status.

data_elements.name: effect-polarity
data_elements.description: Whether the assessed effect is treated as downside, upside or two-sided under the pinned criteria.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are reference and pin fields carried on the host record; they produce no separable document. Reproducing the referenced risk statement here would fork the authoritative text owned by the risk entity model, so the binding stores an identifier, a revision token and a digest rather than a copy.

findings.name: Objective, asset, process and context anchors
findings.description: Records what the risk is assessed against - objectives, assets, processes, organizational units, fixed contextual conditions and applicable jurisdiction or site - as references, so the estimate is interpretable and comparable only within its declared anchor set. Master data for each anchor belongs to its own registry.

questions.text: Which objectives does this assessment measure the effect of uncertainty against?
answer_data: objective version or planning period reference

questions.text: Which assets, processes or organizational units are inside the assessed exposure?
Which contextual conditions were treated as fixed rather than assessed for this estimate?
answer_data: reference to the context description in force

questions.text: Where anchors are jurisdiction-specific or site-specific, how is the applicable location recorded?

data_elements.name: assessment-anchor-set
data_elements.description: The complete set of resolvable anchors this assessment is scoped against; at least one anchor must resolve for the context to be valid.

data_elements.name: objective-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an objective whose achievement the assessed uncertainty affects.

data_elements.name: asset-or-process-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an asset, process, system or service inside the assessed exposure.

data_elements.name: context-condition-statement
data_elements.description: A contextual condition held fixed for this assessment, whose change invalidates the estimate.

data_elements.name: applicable-jurisdiction-or-site
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction, site or facility whose rules or conditions make the anchor set location-specific.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Anchors are pure reference data pointing into objective, asset, process and organizational registries owned elsewhere. Materialising them as a local artifact would duplicate master data and create a second, silently diverging copy of records this model has no authority to maintain.

findings.name: Risk source, event and consequence anchors
findings.description: Carries references to the risk source or threat source, the single event or event class whose likelihood is quantified, and the consequences included in the impact estimate, together with named exclusions. This makes likelihood and impact attach to a stated causal chain rather than to a bare label.

questions.text: Which risk source or threat source does this estimate attribute the event to?
answer_data: risk source or threat source reference
source characterization such as adversarial or non-adversarial

questions.text: Which single event or event class does the likelihood dimension quantify?
answer_data: distinction between initiating event and consequential event

questions.text: Which consequences are inside the impact estimate and which named consequences are excluded?
answer_data: order of consequence such as primary or secondary

questions.text: Which vulnerability or predisposing condition is assumed present for the event to occur?
answer_data: status of that condition at the as-of time

questions.text: Which external threat or hazard catalogue entry is cited, and under which catalogue version?

data_elements.name: risk-source-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the risk source or threat source the event is attributed to.

data_elements.name: event-reference-or-statement
data_elements.description: Reference to, or statement of, the event or event class whose likelihood is quantified.

data_elements.name: consequence-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a consequence included in the impact estimate.

data_elements.name: excluded-consequence-statement
data_elements.description: A consequence deliberately outside the impact estimate, recorded so the omission is visible rather than inferred.

data_elements.name: predisposing-condition-statement
data_elements.description: Vulnerability, weakness or predisposing condition assumed present for the event to occur.

data_elements.name: threat-catalogue-identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a cited external threat or hazard catalogue entry, with its naming system and version.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The causal chain is expressed as short reference and statement fields on the host record. Full source, threat and consequence descriptions belong to threat catalogues and consequence registries; carrying only identifiers plus catalogue version keeps the mixin embeddable and avoids asserting ownership of catalogue content.

layers.name: Classification, scope and method framing
layers.description: Fields that pin the interpretive frame of the estimate: category values against a versioned taxonomy, the assessment boundary and time structure, and the criteria set, method, technique and expression mode under which any recorded value must be read.

findings.name: Category assignment with taxonomy and version pin
findings.description: Pins the category values used to classify the referenced risk within this assessment context, together with the taxonomy scheme identifier and version, because category labels are only comparable inside one pinned scheme and category lists differ materially between frameworks.

questions.text: Which taxonomy scheme and version supplies the category values asserted here?
Which category values are asserted, and is more than one concurrent categorization permitted?
answer_data: primary category designation where one is required

questions.text: How is a category value mapped when the adopting Dimension and an external framework use different schemes?
answer_data: mapping fidelity such as exact, broader, narrower or unmapped

questions.text: Who is authorized to change a pinned category value after an estimate has been recorded against it?
answer_data: record of the prior pinned value

data_elements.name: taxonomy-system-identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier or namespace of the category scheme supplying the asserted values.

data_elements.name: taxonomy-version
data_elements.description: Immutable version token of the category scheme in force for this assessment context.

data_elements.name: category-value
data_elements.description: A category value asserted against the pinned scheme.

data_elements.name: category-mapping-note
data_elements.description: Reference to a crosswalk plus the fidelity of the mapping when values are restated in another scheme.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Category pins are coded field values plus a scheme and version reference. The taxonomy document itself is owned and published by its issuing registry, so this model stores the pin and any crosswalk reference rather than a local copy of the scheme.

findings.name: Assessment scope, horizon and time structure
findings.description: Declares what the assessment covers and for how long: the assessment boundary and its exclusions, the time horizon over which likelihood is expressed, the as-of time of the assessed state, the time the estimate was recorded, the validity or review-due time, and the decision the assessment was produced for.

questions.text: What is the declared boundary of this assessment and what is explicitly excluded from it?
Over what time horizon is the likelihood or frequency dimension expressed?
answer_data: whether the horizon is rolling or fixed

questions.text: What are the as-of time of the assessed state and the time the estimate was recorded, and do they differ?
answer_data: as-of time of the assessed state
explanation where the gap is material

questions.text: Until when is this assessment treated as current, and what triggers an out-of-date state?
Which decision or reporting purpose was this assessment produced for?
answer_data: limits on reuse for other purposes

data_elements.name: assessment-scope-statement
data_elements.description: Declared boundary of what this assessment covers.

data_elements.name: scope-exclusion-statement
data_elements.description: An element deliberately outside the assessment boundary, with the reason for exclusion.

data_elements.name: likelihood-time-horizon
data_elements.description: Period over which the likelihood or frequency dimension is expressed.

data_elements.name: assessment-as-of-time
data_elements.description: Time of the assessed state that the estimate describes, recorded in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: assessment-recorded-time
data_elements.description: Time the estimate was produced and stored, held separately from the as-of time.

data_elements.name: validity-or-review-due-time
data_elements.description: Time after which the assessment is treated as no longer current absent revalidation.

data_elements.name: assessment-purpose
data_elements.description: The decision or reporting purpose the assessment was produced to serve.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scope, horizon and the three distinct time fields are structured attributes of the assessment context itself and must remain queryable alongside every estimate. Splitting them into a separate document would let a value be read without its horizon, which is the specific failure this finding exists to prevent.

findings.name: Criteria, method and expression-mode pin
findings.description: Pins the risk criteria set, the assessment method or technique and their versions, plus the expression mode under which values are recorded, so that a level of risk stays interpretable and so that comparison can be refused when pins differ. The mixin references method definitions and never restates technique semantics.

questions.text: Which risk criteria set, at which version, defines the scales and thresholds used here?
Which assessment technique or method was applied, and where is its normative definition held?
answer_data: locator of the normative technique definition

questions.text: Is the expression qualitative, ordinal, semi-quantitative, quantitative, probabilistic or scenario-based?
answer_data: scale type such as nominal, ordinal, interval or ratio
permitted operations for that scale type

questions.text: What must match before two records assessed under different pins may be compared?
answer_data: action when pins do not match

questions.text: Who approved the criteria set for use in this assessment context?

data_elements.name: criteria-set-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned criteria set defining scales and thresholds for this context.

data_elements.name: criteria-set-version
data_elements.description: Immutable version token of the criteria set in force.

data_elements.name: method-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assessment method or technique applied.

data_elements.name: method-version
data_elements.description: Version or edition of the applied method or technique.

data_elements.name: expression-mode
data_elements.description: How values are expressed: qualitative, ordinal, semi-quantitative, quantitative, probabilistic or scenario-based.

data_elements.name: method-definition-locator
data_elements.description: Resolvable locator of the normative definition of the pinned technique, held by its publisher.

artifacts.name: Pinned criteria and method record
artifacts.description: A retrievable snapshot or resolvable citation of the criteria set, its scales and thresholds, and the method definition in force for this assessment context, sufficient for a reader to re-read a recorded level of risk long after the live criteria have been revised.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative criteria-set identifier issued by the owning criteria registry; where none exists, a governed IRI for the criteria set combined with its immutable version token; where neither exists, a UUID assigned by the adopting Dimension bound to a content digest. A criteria review date or cycle name is never used as the identifier.

bundles.name: Estimation and evidential basis
bundles.description: The dimension declarations that give likelihood and consequence their meaning, the inherent estimate and its exclusion statement, and the assumptions, information sources, estimation basis and uncertainty qualification that make the estimate falsifiable.
bundles.rationale: NIST SP 800-30 separates likelihood of initiation, likelihood of adverse impact and level of impact, and requires assumptions, constraints and information sources to be documented with results. The AI RMF records that risk measurement is genuinely hard and that some risks are emergent or poorly measurable. An estimate presented without its dimension declarations and its basis is therefore not defensible context.

layers.name: Likelihood and consequence dimension declarations
layers.description: Declares the form, unit and scale of each side of the estimate, admitting ordinal bands, probabilities, frequencies, distributions and multi-dimensional impact without imposing any single matrix.

findings.name: Likelihood and frequency expression
findings.description: Declares how the likelihood side is expressed - ordinal band, probability, frequency per unit time, qualitative descriptor or distribution - with its unit, scale reference, horizon dependency and the operations its scale type forbids.

questions.text: In what form is likelihood expressed and against which scale or unit?
Does this record separate likelihood of event occurrence from likelihood of adverse consequence?
answer_data: likelihood of adverse impact given occurrence
whether the two are combined and how

questions.text: If a range or distribution is used, which parameters, bounds and confidence level are stored?
answer_data: confidence level associated with the range

questions.text: Which operations on the likelihood value are prohibited by its scale type?
answer_data: prohibited operations such as multiplication or averaging of ordinals

data_elements.name: likelihood-expression-mode
data_elements.description: Form in which the likelihood side is expressed for this record.

data_elements.name: likelihood-ordinal-band
data_elements.description: Scale-referenced ordinal band value, stored as a code so that arithmetic is not implied by the encoding.

data_elements.name: likelihood-quantitative-value
data_elements.description: Probability or frequency value with its unit, where a quantitative or probabilistic mode is pinned.

data_elements.name: likelihood-scale-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the scale definition in the pinned criteria set that gives the value meaning.

data_elements.name: likelihood-decomposition
data_elements.description: Separate storage of likelihood of occurrence and likelihood of adverse impact where the pinned method distinguishes them.

data_elements.name: likelihood-distribution-parameters
data_elements.description: Parameters and bounds of a distribution or range representation of likelihood.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Dimension declarations must be stored with the value they qualify, because a likelihood detached from its mode, unit and scale is the exact defect this finding guards against. Any supporting analysis output is captured by the derivation record in the basis finding rather than duplicated here.

findings.name: Impact and consequence dimensions
findings.description: Declares the impact side, which may be multi-dimensional across financial, safety, health, fundamental-rights, environmental, operational, reputational and regulatory effects, each with its own scale, and states how or whether dimensions are combined and which parties bear each consequence.

questions.text: Which impact dimensions are scored, and on which scale is each one expressed?
How are multiple impact dimensions combined, or is combination explicitly withheld?
answer_data: statement that no combined value is asserted

questions.text: Are safety, health, environmental or fundamental-rights harms represented as first-class dimensions rather than monetized proxies?
answer_data: legal or policy basis requiring the dimension
monetization statement where a proxy is used

questions.text: Which affected parties bear each recorded consequence?
answer_data: whether the party is internal or external

questions.text: How are secondary or downstream consequences distinguished from primary consequences?
answer_data: basis for treating a loss as secondary
whether secondary effects are inside the estimate

data_elements.name: impact-dimension-set
data_elements.description: The set of impact dimensions scored in this assessment context.

data_elements.name: impact-value-per-dimension
data_elements.description: Value recorded for one impact dimension together with its scale reference and unit.

data_elements.name: impact-combination-rule
data_elements.description: Declared rule for combining dimensions, or an explicit statement that no combined value is asserted.

data_elements.name: affected-party-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a party bearing a recorded consequence, including external and vulnerable groups where relevant.

data_elements.name: consequence-order
data_elements.description: Whether a recorded consequence is primary or secondary or downstream under the pinned method.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Impact dimensions are structured values that must travel with the estimate and stay queryable per dimension. Externalising them would encourage reading a single headline severity without its dimension set, and the affected-party detail is a reference into party registries owned elsewhere.

findings.name: Inherent estimate and its exclusion statement
findings.description: Records the estimate produced before, or excluding, the effect of the referenced controls, together with an explicit statement of what inherent was taken to mean, because the term is not uniformly defined and some authorities do not require it at all. Omission must be recorded with a ground rather than left implicit.

questions.text: What definition of inherent or gross risk was used, and which control effects were excluded from it?
answer_data: whether any controls were assumed present

questions.text: What is the recorded inherent level, and how does it relate the likelihood and impact dimensions?
Was an inherent estimate produced at all, and if not, on what documented ground was it omitted?
answer_data: approving role reference for the omission

questions.text: What derivation or evidence supports the inherent value?
answer_data: identity of the analyst or tool that produced it

data_elements.name: inherent-definition-statement
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of what inherent meant in this context, including which control effects were excluded.

data_elements.name: inherent-estimate-value
data_elements.description: The inherent estimate expressed under the pinned criteria, dimension by dimension.

data_elements.name: inherent-estimate-state
data_elements.description: Whether an inherent estimate is present, is an initial characterization, or was deliberately not produced.

data_elements.name: inherent-omission-ground
data_elements.description: Documented ground for omitting an inherent estimate where none was produced.

data_elements.name: inherent-derivation-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the derivation record supporting the inherent value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The inherent estimate is a role-tagged value slot on the assessment context, and its exclusion statement must be inseparable from it. The supporting derivation is captured once as an artifact under the basis finding, so declaring a second artifact here would duplicate the same evidence object.

layers.name: Assessment basis, assumptions and uncertainty
layers.description: The evidential qualification of the estimate: assumptions that must hold, the information sources and their currency, whether the value came from judgement, data or a model, the constraints on the analysis, and how much confidence and precision the result can bear.

findings.name: Assumptions, data basis and uncertainty qualification
findings.description: Captures the assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind and analysis constraints behind the estimate, together with confidence or data-quality grading, uncertainty representation, unmeasurable aspects and precision caveats. This is what allows a reader to judge whether a value rests on incident history, expert judgement, modelled data or a vendor claim, and how far it may be trusted.

questions.text: Which explicit assumptions must hold for this estimate to remain valid?
Which information sources and datasets were used, and how current were they at the as-of time?
answer_data: known gaps in the source coverage

questions.text: Was the estimate elicited from expert judgement, derived from historical data, or produced by a model run?
answer_data: number and qualification of estimators where elicited
model or tool identity and version where modelled

questions.text: What confidence or data-quality grade is attached to this estimate, and on which scale?
answer_data: uncertainty representation such as range, interval, distribution or narrative caveat

questions.text: What precision may downstream consumers infer from the stored notation, and which aspects are effectively unmeasurable?

data_elements.name: assumption-statement
data_elements.description: An explicit assumption whose falsification would change or invalidate the estimate.

data_elements.name: critical-assumption-flag
data_elements.description: Marks the assumption whose falsification would most change the recorded result.

data_elements.name: information-source-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a dataset, observation set, report or elicitation used as an input.

data_elements.name: data-currency-time
data_elements.description: Currency time of an information source, recorded separately from the assessment as-of and recording times.

data_elements.name: estimation-basis-kind
data_elements.description: Whether the estimate is judgement-elicited, data-derived, model-produced or a declared hybrid.

data_elements.name: analysis-constraint-statement
data_elements.description: A constraint on the analysis such as limited time, access or data availability.

data_elements.name: confidence-grade
data_elements.description: Confidence or data-quality grade with its scale reference.

data_elements.name: uncertainty-representation
data_elements.description: How uncertainty is expressed: range, interval, distribution, narrative caveat or none stated.

data_elements.name: unmeasurable-aspect-statement
data_elements.description: Aspect of the risk acknowledged as emergent, inscrutable or not measurable to the implied precision.

data_elements.name: precision-caveat
data_elements.description: Statement limiting the precision downstream consumers may infer from the stored notation.

artifacts.name: Assessment basis statement
artifacts.description: A retained statement of purpose, scope, assumptions, constraints and information sources for one assessment context, corresponding to the documented content that a risk assessment report is expected to carry alongside its results.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier issued by the assessment system of record where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI under the adopting Dimension's namespace; otherwise a UUID assigned by the adopting Dimension and bound to the assessment-context identifier plus its recorded time. The assessment date alone is never the identifier.

artifacts.name: Estimate derivation record
artifacts.description: A record of the inputs, technique run and intermediate results that produced a recorded estimate, retained so the value can be re-read and challenged without re-running the analysis, and so the origin of a characterization is traceable to a human or automated actor.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier issued by the analysis system of record where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI under the adopting Dimension's namespace; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension and ordered by recording time. A review cycle name or period label is never used as the identifier.

bundles.name: Residual position and comparability
bundles.description: The post-control estimate with its control linkage and change explanation, the comparison against referenced appetite or tolerance with its governance stamps, and the comparability, aggregation and scenario-dependence controls that stop values from being combined when their pins do not match.
bundles.rationale: Residual risk is the concept that closes the risk-control loop: OSCAL expresses it as an adjusted characterization citing mitigating factors linked to implementation statements, the AI RMF requires residual risk to be documented and disclosed, and EU law requires residual risk per hazard to be judged acceptable. Roll-up guidance stages registers into an enterprise profile, which makes an explicit comparability gate necessary rather than optional.

layers.name: Residual estimate, control linkage and appetite comparison
layers.description: Fields that record the post-control estimate, the controls relied on and the effectiveness determinations cited for them, the explanation of change, and the outcome of comparing the residual position against a referenced tolerance statement.

findings.name: Residual estimate, control linkage and change explanation
findings.description: Records the estimate after the referenced controls are taken into account, the control references relied on, the effectiveness determinations cited for each of them, which dimension changed, and why. Effectiveness is cited by reference and is produced by the control assessment model; this finding never derives, revises or re-opens it.

questions.text: Which controls were relied on when producing the residual estimate, and by which reference?
answer_data: scope of reliance placed on each control

questions.text: Which effectiveness determination is cited for each relied-on control, and who produced it?
answer_data: determination outcome as recorded by its owner

questions.text: Which dimension changed between the inherent and residual estimates - likelihood, consequence, or both?
How is the residual value marked as an adjusted rather than an initial characterization?
What is recorded when a control is referenced but no effectiveness determination exists for it?

data_elements.name: residual-estimate-value
data_elements.description: The residual estimate expressed under the same pinned criteria and dimensions as the inherent estimate.

data_elements.name: relied-on-control-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a control relied on when producing the residual estimate, resolving into the control implementation model.

data_elements.name: cited-effectiveness-determination-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an effectiveness determination produced by the control assessment model and cited here without restatement.

data_elements.name: reliance-without-determination-flag
data_elements.description: Marks reliance on a control for which no current effectiveness determination is available.

data_elements.name: changed-dimension
data_elements.description: Which dimension the control effect changed: likelihood, consequence or both.

data_elements.name: residual-change-explanation
data_elements.description: Narrative explanation of what changed between the inherent and residual estimates and why.

data_elements.name: estimate-characterization-state
data_elements.description: Whether this characterization is initial as first identified or adjusted after control effects were taken into account.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The residual value, its control references and its change explanation are inline fields of the assessment context. The evidence objects behind them - implementation statements and effectiveness determinations - are artifacts of the control implementation and control assessment models, so declaring a local artifact here would claim ownership of documents this model may only cite.

findings.name: Appetite or tolerance reference and comparison outcome
findings.description: References the appetite or tolerance statement in force, records the outcome of comparing the residual estimate against it, and stamps who recorded the comparison and which acceptance or authorization decision, if any, was taken elsewhere. Setting, approving and enforcing appetite are not performed here.

questions.text: Which appetite or tolerance statement, at which version, was the residual estimate compared against?
What is the recorded comparison outcome and on which scale is it expressed?
answer_data: distance to threshold where the scale supports it
scale reference used for the comparison

questions.text: Who recorded the comparison, and which decision record shows the residual position being accepted?
answer_data: role reference that recorded the comparison

questions.text: What is recorded when no applicable tolerance statement exists for the pinned criteria?
Which downstream consumers may read the comparison outcome without access to the underlying estimates?
answer_data: caveats that must accompany the release

data_elements.name: appetite-or-tolerance-statement-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the appetite or tolerance statement in force for this comparison.

data_elements.name: appetite-statement-version
data_elements.description: Version token of the referenced appetite or tolerance statement.

data_elements.name: tolerance-threshold-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the specific threshold or tolerance line applied to a dimension.

data_elements.name: comparison-outcome
data_elements.description: Recorded outcome of comparing the residual estimate with the referenced tolerance, including a no-applicable-tolerance value.

data_elements.name: comparison-recorded-by
data_elements.description: Reference to the role or actor that recorded the comparison outcome.

data_elements.name: acceptance-decision-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an acceptance, authorization or exception decision recorded in the model that owns such decisions.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The comparison is a small set of reference and outcome fields. The appetite statement is a governance document owned by enterprise risk governance, and the acceptance decision is an authorization record owned by the decision model, so this finding carries pointers and an outcome code rather than any local document.

layers.name: Comparability, aggregation and scenario dependence
layers.description: The gate that decides whether two assessment contexts may be compared, rolled up or reported together, the caveats any permitted aggregate must carry, and how one risk assessed under several scenarios is represented without collapsing into a single false value.

findings.name: Comparability verdicts, aggregation caveats and scenario dependence
findings.description: Records whether records may be placed on a common scale, which pins failed to match when they may not, which caveats must travel with any permitted aggregate, and how scenario variants and a designated reference case are represented. The model refuses to define a normalization algorithm it has no authority to assert.

questions.text: Under what conditions may two assessment contexts be placed on the same scale?
answer_data: named mismatched pins where the verdict is negative

questions.text: Which caveats must travel with any aggregate produced from these records?
answer_data: permitted aggregation operations for the scale type

questions.text: How is scenario dependence recorded when one risk is assessed under several scenarios?
Which scenario or variant is designated the reference case for reporting, and by which role?
How are records assessed under a superseded criteria version handled in a current roll-up?
answer_data: exclusion from the aggregate where no migration exists

data_elements.name: comparability-verdict
data_elements.description: Whether the compared records are comparable, comparable with caveats, or not comparable.

data_elements.name: mismatched-pin-list
data_elements.description: The specific pins that failed to match, naming criteria set, method, expression mode, scope, horizon or taxonomy.

data_elements.name: aggregation-caveat
data_elements.description: A caveat that must accompany any aggregate or roll-up built from this record.

data_elements.name: scenario-identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a scenario under which this estimate was produced.

data_elements.name: scenario-definition-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned scenario definition owned by the scenario or method registry.

data_elements.name: reference-case-flag
data_elements.description: Marks the scenario variant designated as the reference case for reporting.

data_elements.name: superseded-criteria-handling
data_elements.description: How a record pinned to a withdrawn criteria version is treated in a current roll-up.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Comparability verdicts and caveats are computed conclusions about this record's own fields and must remain attached to it so they cannot be separated from any value they qualify. The aggregate itself is produced and owned by the enterprise reporting model, so no local aggregate artifact is declared.

functions.name: Bind an assessment context to a referenced risk
functions.description: Creates a revision-pinned binding between one host record and one referenced risk, capturing anchors, taxonomy pin, scope, horizon and criteria/method pins. It establishes context only and never creates, alters or advances the referenced risk entity.
inputs: risk reference and exact revision pin
assessment anchor set (objectives, assets, processes, context conditions, jurisdiction or site)
causal anchors (risk source, event, consequences and exclusions)
taxonomy system identifier and version with category values
assessment scope statement, exclusions, likelihood horizon and as-of time
criteria set reference and version, method reference and version, expression mode
outputs: bound assessment-context record with binding validity state set to current
recorded as-of time and recorded time as separate values
rejection result naming any required pin or reference that failed to resolve
preconditions: the risk reference resolves in the model that owns the risk entity
the criteria set and method references resolve at the stated versions
a scope statement and an as-of time are supplied
at least one anchor reference resolves
effects: establishes a stable binding that is invalidated rather than silently re-pointed when the upstream revision changes
sets binding validity state and records the detection time when supersession is later observed
does not create, modify, approve or advance the referenced risk entity or its register status

functions.name: Record an estimate under a pinned method
functions.description: Stores an estimate in either the inherent or residual role exactly as produced by the pinned method, together with its dimensions, units, scale references and expression mode. It performs no method-specific computation and invents no scale semantics.
inputs: bound assessment context
estimate role (inherent or residual)
likelihood expression with mode, unit or scale reference and any distribution parameters
impact values per declared dimension with their scale references
characterization state (initial or adjusted) and derivation reference
outputs: stored estimate with role tag, characterization state and full dimension declarations
validation errors where the expression does not match the pinned criteria scale
recorded time distinct from the assessment as-of time
preconditions: a criteria set and method pin are present with versions
the expression mode is declared and the referenced scale resolves
for the inherent role, an inherent definition statement or a documented omission ground is present
effects: stores values only in the form the pinned method produced them
stores ordinal values as scale-referenced codes so that arithmetic is not implied by the encoding
refuses operations the declared scale type does not support
never derives a value the pinned method did not produce

functions.name: Compare inherent and residual estimates
functions.description: Records the difference between an inherent and a residual estimate, the dimensions that changed, the controls relied on and the effectiveness determinations cited, and the outcome of comparing the residual position with a referenced tolerance statement.
inputs: inherent estimate and residual estimate for the same bound context
relied-on control references and cited effectiveness determination references
appetite or tolerance statement reference and version
outputs: changed-dimension set with per-dimension before and after values
comparison outcome against the referenced tolerance, including a no-applicable-tolerance value
preconditions: both estimates share criteria set, method, expression mode, scope, horizon and taxonomy pins
the residual estimate carries an adjusted characterization state
each cited effectiveness determination resolves, or a reliance-without-determination flag is set
effects: records the delta and its explanation as assessment context
cites control effectiveness determinations without computing, revising or re-opening them
records a comparison outcome without granting, approving or enforcing acceptance of the residual position
refuses to produce a comparison when the pin sets differ, returning the mismatched pins instead

functions.name: Explain assumptions and evidential basis
functions.description: Assembles and records the assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind, analysis constraints and uncertainty qualification behind an estimate, and emits the basis statement and derivation record artifacts.
inputs: assumption statements with critical-assumption flags
information source references and their data currency times
estimation basis kind and, where modelled, tool identity and version
analysis constraint statements
confidence grade, uncertainty representation and precision caveat
outputs: estimate derivation record artifact where a derivation exists
inline uncertainty qualification attached to the estimate
list of assumptions whose falsification would most change the result
preconditions: at least one assumption statement is supplied
an estimation basis kind and an uncertainty representation are declared
effects: makes the estimate falsifiable by naming what it depends on
records data currency separately from the assessment as-of and recorded times
does not evaluate, score or rank the quality of the cited sources beyond the declared grade

functions.name: Check comparability before comparison, reuse or aggregation
functions.description: Compares the pin sets of two or more assessment-context records against a requested comparison or aggregation operation and returns a verdict, the mismatched pins and the caveat set that any permitted result must carry.
inputs: two or more assessment-context records with their pin sets
requested operation (pairwise comparison, trend reuse, or aggregation)
scale type and permitted operations from the pinned criteria
outputs: comparability verdict: comparable, comparable with caveats, or not comparable
named list of mismatched pins where the verdict is negative
caveat set to attach to any permitted result
handling code for records pinned to a withdrawn criteria version
preconditions: each record carries criteria, method, expression-mode, scope, horizon and taxonomy pins
the scale type of each value is resolvable
effects: blocks silent aggregation of ordinal or differently pinned estimates
attaches caveats that downstream consumers are prohibited from stripping
asserts no normalization or roll-up algorithm; the enterprise reporting model owns any aggregate it chooses to build under the returned verdict

composition.target: WM-KNW-015 - Risk / Opportunity entity and lifecycle
composition.purpose: The parent model owns risk identity, statement, register membership, status and lifecycle transitions. This mixin attaches one assessment context to a pinned revision of that entity, carries only its own binding validity state, and reproduces no risk lifecycle or register operations.

composition.target: Host record of the adopting Dimension that carries risk-control linkage fields
composition.purpose: Defines how this field group is embedded on a host entity, event or decision record so a Dimension can carry a defensible assessment context without standing up a separate register.

composition.target: Control implementation and control assessment records (control register, implemented requirements, effectiveness determinations)
composition.purpose: Supplies control identity, implementation statements and effectiveness determinations that the residual estimate cites. Assessment procedures, objectives, methods and the production of determinations remain wholly with that model; this mixin carries only the reference and the reliance parameters specific to this assessment.

composition.target: Risk criteria and assessment-method registry (criteria sets, scales, thresholds, technique definitions)
composition.purpose: Supplies the versioned criteria scales and technique definitions that this mixin pins. The mixin stores the pin, the version token and the expression mode; it never defines, parameterizes or re-implements technique semantics.

Supplies the versioned thresholds the residual estimate is compared against. Determining, approving, publishing and enforcing appetite and tolerance remain with enterprise governance; this mixin records the reference and the comparison outcome only.

composition.target: Objective, asset, process and organizational-unit registries
composition.purpose: Supplies the anchors an assessment is scoped against. The mixin holds anchor references and assessment-specific scoping parameters; master data, anchor lifecycle and ownership stay in those registries.

composition.target: Acceptance, authorization and exception decision records
composition.purpose: Receives a pointer from the comparison outcome to the decision in which a residual position was accepted. Decision authority, approval workflow and the validity of the decision belong to that model; this mixin never grants or derives acceptance.

composition.target: Risk treatment, remediation and plan-of-action records
composition.purpose: Consumes the residual position as an input to treatment planning. Treatment option selection, milestones, scheduling, cost and closure are owned there and are not represented in this field group.

Supplies observations and evidence cited as information sources for an estimate. Evidence collection, assessment execution and result logging are owned there; this mixin cites references and records their currency.

External alignment for naming and selecting the applied technique. The mixin records which technique and version were used and makes no conformance claim to the standard, whose normative text is not reproduced here.

composition.target: NIST IR 8286 cybersecurity risk register and risk detail record schemas
composition.purpose: External alignment for register field naming and for enterprise roll-up expectations. Adoption is a projection of this field group into that schema, not a conformance claim, and the register's own lifecycle stays with the register model.

composition.target: OSCAL Assessment Results risk characterization (characterization, facet, mitigating-factor)
composition.purpose: External alignment for expressing initial versus adjusted characterizations and control-based mitigating factors in machine-readable form. The mixin maps its fields onto those assemblies without adopting the assessment-results model's observation, risk-log or remediation semantics.

composition.target: The Open Group Risk Taxonomy (O-RT) Version 3.1
composition.purpose: Alignment for a frequency-and-magnitude decomposition where a Dimension pins a FAIR-family method. The mixin carries the pin and the resulting values; the taxonomy and its analysis process stay with the standard and its companion Risk Analysis standard.

composition.target: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 9 risk management system for high-risk AI systems
composition.purpose: Jurisdiction-scoped alignment evidencing a legal requirement that residual risk per hazard be judged acceptable and that estimation cover reasonably foreseeable misuse. The mixin records the reference and the comparison outcome; conformity assessment and enforcement are outside it.

owner_package_requirements: Name a single accountable owner for the criteria and method pin vocabulary used by adopting records; the owner is a Dimension role, and this model neither appoints nor supersedes it.

Publish every criteria set, scale definition and threshold with an immutable version token before any estimate is recorded against it, and retain withdrawn versions for as long as records pinned to them survive.

Declare which referenced models supply risk, control, effectiveness-determination, tolerance, objective and evidence identifiers, and keep those references resolvable for the full retention period of the assessment records that cite them.
Register the comparability policy that decides when estimates under different pins may be compared or aggregated, and the role authorized to grant an exception to it.
Declare the redaction and classification policy for consequence and affected-party fields before the field group is embedded on any host record.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Field names are carried under a Dimension-owned namespace qualified by the model identifier WM-XCT-027 and the navigation path NAV.XCT.RSK. Values drawn from external schemes - taxonomy codes, technique names, threat catalogue entries, control identifiers, OSCAL facet systems - retain their issuing system's namespace and version and are never re-minted locally. Local identifiers are minted only for the assessment context itself and for artifacts this model owns.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-027 under nav path NAV.XCT.RSK with domain tag XCT.RSK
The adopting Dimension's criteria and assessment-method registry, which owns criteria sets, scales, thresholds and technique references
External alignment registries: the IEC 31010 technique catalogue, the NIST IR 8286 risk register and risk detail record schemas, and OSCAL assessment-results facet systems

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the semantic field set, not any serialization. JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git-tracked files, MCP resources and MongoDB documents are projections and must round-trip identical field values, pins and caveats.

An estimate is canonically stored together with its expression mode, unit or scale reference and complete pin set; a bare value without its pins is not a valid canonical estimate and must be rejected on read as well as on write.

All time values are canonicalized to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. The as-of time of the assessed state, the time the estimate was recorded, and the currency time of each information source are distinct canonical fields even when their values coincide.
Ordinal values are canonicalized as scale-referenced codes, never as bare integers, so that no arithmetic is implied by the encoding.
Comparability caveats are canonically part of the estimate record, not a presentation-layer annotation.
patch_rules: A published estimate is corrected by a superseding assessment-context record that cites the prior record; in-place mutation of a published estimate value is not permitted.
Changing any pin - criteria set, method, expression mode, scope, horizon or taxonomy - constitutes a new assessment context rather than a patch to the existing one.
Non-semantic corrections to narrative statements may be patched in place, recording the editing role reference and the patch time, provided no value, pin or caveat changes.
Binding validity state may be updated in place when an upstream revision is superseded, because that records an observation about the reference rather than a change to the assessment.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional impact dimension, caveat field or reference field is backward compatible; removing a pin field, re-typing it, or changing the meaning of a scale code is breaking.
Consumers encountering an unrecognised expression mode, scale reference or taxonomy version must treat the record as not comparable rather than coercing it to a default numeric scale.
Alignment mappings to external schemes are versioned independently and may be revised without changing this model's version, provided the mapping fidelity is restated.
A projection that cannot carry the pin set or the caveat set is not a conforming projection of this model, regardless of storage technology.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record that owns the artifact - for example the assessment system's report identifier or the criteria registry's criteria-set identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI from a normative registry or a controlled namespace, used only where no authoritative master-system identifier exists.

UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, bound to the assessment-context identifier and to a content digest; a date, review cycle name, fiscal period or version label is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Event time - the as-of time of the state the estimate describes - is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, which is when the estimate was produced and when it was stored; where a validity or review-due time and an information-source currency time exist, each is a further distinct field and none may be inferred from another.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts - assessment basis statements and estimate derivation records - are named by the stable assessment-context identifier plus a monotonically increasing sequence value issued at recording time. The sequence carries no date, period or cycle component, gaps are permitted, and a retired sequence value is never reused.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest together with the identifier and version of the pinned criteria set and method. A digest mismatch, an unresolvable pin or a withdrawn criteria version marks the artifact unverifiable, which blocks its use in any comparison, reuse or aggregation until it is restated or explicitly excepted by the comparability reviewer.

policies: No estimate is published without its complete pin set; a level of risk detached from its criteria set, method, expression mode and horizon is treated as an unusable value rather than a low-quality one.
Inherent and residual estimates are compared only when their pins match; otherwise the comparison is recorded as not permitted and the mismatched pins are named.
This model records references to control effectiveness determinations, acceptance decisions and audit entries; it never derives, revises, enforces or re-opens them.
No numeric risk matrix, default likelihood band or default impact scale is defined by this model; every scale is supplied by reference from the criteria registry.
Aggregation carries the caveat set produced by the comparability check, and downstream consumers may not strip those caveats when re-presenting a value.

Omission is recorded explicitly: a missing inherent estimate, a missing effectiveness determination and a missing tolerance statement each have a declared field rather than being represented by absence.

read: Reading an estimate returns the value together with its pin set, uncertainty qualification and comparability caveats as one indivisible response; partial responses that omit pins or caveats are non-conforming.

Resolution of referenced risk, control, effectiveness-determination, tolerance and evidence identifiers is delegated to the owning models; this model returns the reference and its last observed resolution state without asserting the target's current status.
Superseded assessment contexts remain readable and are returned marked with the superseding record reference, so historical decisions stay explicable.
create: An assessment context is created only with a resolvable risk reference, an exact revision pin, a criteria and method pin with versions, a scope statement and at least one resolvable anchor.
Creation records the as-of time of the assessed state and the recording time as separate RFC 3339 values with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
Creating an assessment context never creates, activates or advances the referenced risk entity, control record or decision record.
update: Pin changes, estimate value changes and scope changes are effected by superseding records rather than in-place edits, preserving the prior record and its citations.
Binding validity state is updated in place when the pinned risk revision is superseded upstream, without altering any recorded estimate value or caveat.
Narrative corrections are patched in place with an editing role reference and a patch time, and may not change a value, pin, caveat or comparison outcome.
delete: Assessment-context records are not hard-deleted while any decision, authorization, report or aggregate still cites them; they are tombstoned with the disposition reason, the deciding role reference and the recorded time, retaining the identifier, the pin set and the supersession links so that citations remain explicable.

Retention periods, legal hold and disposition schedules for these records are set and executed by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy and, in regulated contexts, by the authority that mandated the assessment; this model defines the tombstone shape but does not own retention execution.

Deletion of a referenced risk entity, control record, effectiveness determination, evidence record or acceptance decision is owned by those models; on such deletion this model marks its local binding as dangling and blocks further comparison, and it never propagates deletion upstream or downstream.

Personal data appearing in narrative assumption, affected-party or consequence fields is redacted under the adopting Dimension's privacy policy while the tombstone, the identifier and the pin set are retained; redaction is recorded as a disposition event rather than as a patch.

Artifacts owned by this model - basis statements and derivation records - follow the same tombstone-and-retain rule; artifacts owned by referenced models are never deleted by this model, only dereferenced.

roles.name: Assessment context owner
responsibilities: Maintain the binding to the correct risk reference and revision and act on supersession signals.
Ensure every required pin is present, versioned and resolvable before an estimate is recorded.
Mark stale, dangling or withdrawn contexts and initiate supersession when a pin changes.

roles.name: Assessor or analyst
responsibilities: Produce estimates strictly under the pinned method and record them in the form the method produced.
Record assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind and analysis constraints.
State uncertainty, confidence and precision caveats, including aspects acknowledged as unmeasurable.
Never adjust scale semantics or substitute a different method without creating a new assessment context.

roles.name: Criteria and method steward
responsibilities: Publish and version criteria sets, scales, thresholds and technique references used by adopting records.
Withdraw superseded criteria with a migration or restatement note and retain withdrawn versions.
Approve criteria sets for use in specific contexts and record the approval scope and time.

roles.name: Comparability reviewer
responsibilities: Apply the comparability check before any comparison, trend reuse or roll-up.
Approve or refuse aggregation, naming mismatched pins where refused, and record the caveat set.
Decide the handling of records pinned to withdrawn criteria versions and grant documented exceptions.

roles.name: Records and retention custodian
responsibilities: Apply retention schedules, legal hold, tombstoning and redaction under the adopting Dimension's policy.
Preserve identifiers, pin sets and supersession links on tombstoned records so citations stay explicable.
Coordinate with the owning models when a referenced record is deleted upstream.

access.default_rule: Read access is granted at the narrowest scope that satisfies the requesting role's stated purpose, and every read returns pins, uncertainty qualification and comparability caveats alongside any value. Write access is limited to the assessment context owner and the named assessor for the open, unpublished revision; once published, change is by supersession only.
exceptions: Where impact dimensions carry personal, safety-sensitive or security-sensitive detail, the consequence and affected-party fields may be restricted to named roles while the comparison outcome and its caveats remain readable to reporting consumers.

Basis statements and estimate derivation records may be withheld from broad readership when they contain unpublished vulnerability or commercially sensitive detail; the existence of the artifact, its identifier and its digest remain visible so the record is not silently incomplete.
A legal hold overrides normal restriction and grants the records and retention custodian read access to tombstoned and redacted records for the duration of the hold.
Where a regulator or external assurance provider has a lawful basis, read access may be granted across scopes for a bounded period recorded as an access exception.
audit_requirements: Every create, supersede, tombstone, redaction and comparability refusal is logged with the actor reference, the affected identifiers and a recorded time in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. The audit store, its integrity controls and its retention are owned by the adopting Dimension's audit model; this model states what must be logged, not how the trail is kept.
Reads of restricted consequence, affected-party or basis-artifact fields are logged with the stated purpose and the granting exception.
Grants and revocations of access exceptions are logged with the authorizing role, the bounded period and the scope affected.

read_order: AGENTS.md - read first for Name, Type, the registry identifier and the four locator URLs; it is mandatory even when the field group is stored in MongoDB or exposed only through MCP.
Specification URL - the model boundary, bundles, layers, findings, data elements and the in-scope and out-of-scope statements that govern what may be written here.

Storage type URL - how the field group is projected into the chosen store (embedded document, graph node properties, relational columns, MongoDB collection or Git-tracked file) and how pins and caveats survive that projection.
Interface URL - the read and write surface, including the MCP tool or API binding, and the rule that reads return pins and caveats indivisibly.
Processes URL - the bind, record-estimate, compare, explain-basis and comparability-check procedures with their preconditions, and the supersession and tombstone rules.

coverage.claim: This structure covers the risk-reference binding, assessment framing, estimation, evidential basis, control-linkage reference and residual-comparison surface of WM-XCT-027 as an embeddable field group, grounded in NIST risk-assessment and enterprise risk publications, the OSCAL assessment-results schema, HM Treasury public-authority guidance, the IEC 31010 technique catalogue at catalogue level and the Open Group risk taxonomy at publication level. Control effectiveness evaluation, treatment, acceptance, appetite setting, evidence collection and audit-trail retention are represented as composition links, boundary notes and out-of-scope statements rather than modelled locally. No claim of clause-level conformance to any paywalled standard is made.

checklist.notes: Risk reference plus exact revision pin, taxonomy system identifier, criteria and method references with versions, scenario identifiers and artifact identity strategies.
